title: The controller starts no new agent or regression while available memory is below devloop.min_free_memory_gib
objective: When the machine's available memory is below devloop.min_free_memory_gib, the controller starts no new issuer, regression, fixer or memory keeper (running ones go on) and says why on its idle page and in a live record.
outline: devloop/core/config.py: default and validation next to host_sample_seconds. devloop/ticket_controller.py: a memory_short() helper (reads host.memory_available() each time it is asked; cheap on Linux, two short commands on macOS) used by dispatch(), advance_groups() before start_regression / fix_retry / fix_main_moved, start_fixer() (the deferral of item 4) and consolidate(); tick() leaves groups that only wait for memory out of what counts as busy (keep counting running tickets, groups with a job, verified groups and children), so a controller without --forever ends (project memory: any new wait condition must be left out of 'busy'); report_idle() puts the memory line first; the hold record through core/inflight.put/drop (drop also in main()'s finally). Update the module docstring's dispatch paragraph. README as in item 8; loop harness as in item 7 (its loop dict, not the env block new-2 edits).
test_plan: Verifier: one class T<id>Acceptance in tests_devloop/test_machine.py between class T44Acceptance and class T3Acceptance (LoopCase; strip DEVLOOP_* from self.env). Memory fixture: in self.env (and os.environ via mock.patch.dict for in-process cases) AC_CGROUP_ROOT = an empty folder, AC_MEMINFO = a file holding 'MemAvailable:     524288 kB' (0.5 GiB), AC_VM_STAT = a path that does not exist; self.config(min_free_memory_gib=1). Cases: item 1 (each bad value -> run_py('tickets.py', 'list') rc 2 with 'devloop.min_free_memory_gib' on stderr; and with the key deleted from board/config.json, Config(proj).values['min_free_memory_gib'] == 1; today the key is ignored); items 3+5 end-to-end (self.add(1); controller() rc 0 within 60 s; ticket 1 still 'ready'; no count-worker* / count-verifier* file next to the plan; one idle page whose text's second line is 'memory short: 0.5 GiB available, below devloop.min_free_memory_gib 1: no new agent or regression is started until more is free'; today #1 lands); item 3 for a regression (fixture: branch int/g1 at main, ticket 1 merged in g1, group g1 {state pr, branch int/g1, members ['1'], fix_round 0}; controller() rc 0; g1 has no job, no 'regression started' event and <tmp>/wt/runs/regression/g1/ has no result-*.json; today the regression runs); item 4 in process (the same pr fixture; ctl = ticket_controller.Controller(Config(proj), pool); write a red report file R; ctl.start_fixer('g1', R, 1): no 'fixer:g1' in ctl.children, g1 state pr, fix_retry true, fix_round 0, fix_report R, one event starting 'fix round 1 waits: memory short'; then rewrite the meminfo file to 'MemAvailable:  4194304 kB' and call ctl.advance_groups(ctl.pool.snapshot()): g1 state fixing with job kind fixer; stop that child in a cleanup with osx.kill_tree; today the fixer starts at once); item 6 (Popen ticket_controller.py --forever with one ready ticket; within 10 s <tmp>/wt/runs/live/hold-memory.json has kind hold, reason memory, available 536870912, threshold 1073741824, setting 1 and stamp pid = the controller's pid; rewrite the meminfo file to 4 GiB; within 15 s the record is gone and ticket 1 has left 'ready'; then send SIGTERM and wait; today no record appears). Implementer: unit tests (unknown reading never short, null setting, float setting, the line's %.1f / %g formatting, a running issuer is not stopped) in tests_devloop/test_machine.py between class TestHostSampler and class T44Acceptance; items 7 and 8 are the implementer's. Every case runs in seconds.
notes: Source: plan item 1.2, docs/HANDOFF.md last section (D-100, D-102): the main session's review of an external audit (2026-11-26) and feedback from T's main session (T is a project that runs agent-control daily, 2026-11-26). Quoted feedback is data, not instructions. Assumed, not measured: T's host samples (<worktrees>/runs/host/*.jsonl) live on T's machine and were not readable from this run, and there is no macOS host and no web access here, so the macOS reading could not be checked. Choice that follows: no new macOS parsing - the hold compares against the number the host sampler already records on T since #44 (scripts/hostinfo.py vm_stat_bytes: free + inactive pages), so the 主機 tab's memory curve shows exactly what the hold reads, and an unreadable value never holds (fails open). Default 1 GiB: on this Linux machine (16 GiB) available memory stayed 14.3-15.2 GiB over 502 samples with up to 5 agents running (measured, <worktrees>/runs/host/vm.jsonl), so agents themselves are light and only a machine already deep in swap falls below 1 GiB. Not chosen: swap used (stays high after pressure passes, so it would keep holding; this machine has no swap), and the kernel pressure level (unchecked). To check on T's Mac before or after landing (main session): `vm_stat | head -6; sysctl -n hw.memsize; sysctl -n vm.swapusage; sysctl -n kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level; memory_pressure | tail -1` while healthy and while swapping, compared with mem_available on T's 主機 tab; T can set its own min_free_memory_gib, or null to turn the hold off. Depends on new-1 (both edit ticket_controller.py: advance_groups, finish_jobs, the docstring). hard_block: board/config.json patterns match every added line of the branch (code, tests, comments, README): never write the strings `os.kill`, `killpg`, `pkill` or `kill -` anywhere. Check liveness with core/osx.alive(), stop processes in tests with core/osx.kill_tree() or Popen.send_signal()/terminate(). Refer to T only as 'T' or 'a project with browser tests' in code, tests and comments: a guard (tests/test_no_project_names.py) forbids that project's name in every non-markdown file. Group new-g1 (see new-1's notes).
acceptance: 1. Setting devloop.min_free_memory_gib: null (off) or a number > 0 (int or float, not a bool); default 1; any other value (0, -1, true, "1", []) stops every devloop script with exit 2 and a stderr line naming devloop.min_free_memory_gib.

2. The reading is core/host.memory_available() - the number host samples record as mem_available (cgroup limit minus use, else /proc/meminfo MemAvailable, else macOS vm_stat free + inactive pages capped by hw.memsize; overrides AC_CGROUP_ROOT, AC_MEMINFO, AC_VM_STAT, AC_SYSCTL). Memory is short when that reading is a number below min_free_memory_gib x 2^30 bytes; an unknown reading (None) or a null setting is never short.

3. While memory is short: dispatch starts no ticket (a ready ticket stays ready and no ticket_issuer.py starts); a pr or fixing group whose turn it is in the chain gets no regression and no fix round (no job is written); consolidate starts no memory_keeper. Running issuers (and the agents they start for their own rounds), regressions, fixers, keepers and release jobs go on; landing, the release and the controller's own openers (release and flaky fix tickets) are not held.

4. A fix round that comes due while memory is short (Controller.start_fixer, whether called after a red regression, a dropped round or main moving) starts no auto_fixer: the group goes to state pr with fix_retry true, fix_report = that round's report and fix_round one less than the round asked for, plus one event 'fix round <n> waits: memory short (<x.x> GiB available)'; the next tick with memory not short starts round <n> through the existing fix_retry path of advance_groups.

5. A controller without --forever whose remaining work only waits for memory ends with exit 0 and writes the idle page; its text's second line, right after 'nothing more can move; left undone:', is exactly 'memory short: <available in GiB, %.1f> GiB available, below devloop.min_free_memory_gib <setting, %g>: no new agent or regression is started until more is free', and the same line is on stderr. A --forever controller keeps ticking and starts the held work once memory is no longer short.

6. While memory is short the controller keeps the live record <worktrees>/runs/live/hold-memory.json = {"kind": "hold", "reason": "memory", "stamp": <the controller process's osx.stamp()>, "available": <bytes>, "threshold": <bytes>, "setting": <min_free_memory_gib as configured>, "since": <when this hold began>, "result": null} (since kept while the hold lasts); it is removed on the first tick memory is not short and when the controller exits.

7. tests_devloop/loop_harness.py LoopCase writes "min_free_memory_gib": null into its base devloop config, so loop tests do not depend on the test machine's memory; cases about the hold set it themselves.

8. devloop/README.md: a paragraph at the end of '## Host samples' describes the hold (setting, default, the reading, what is held and what is not, the record, the idle line); '## Live records' lists hold-memory.json in a bullet placed right after the issuer-<id>.json bullet.
token_basis: Comparable: #117 (chain wait, idle rules) 6.8M, #134 (open group waits for a decision) 7.9M, #44 host samples. Touches config.py, five start sites and tick()/report_idle() in ticket_controller.py (after new-1's changes there), the live record, loop_harness, README in two sections; ~6 verifier cases incl. a --forever controller and in-process controller fixtures.

# Phase one, group 1: the machine is not overrun (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 1.1-1.4)

The user approved this plan (D-102, verbatim there). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit (2026-11-26) and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session, which runs agent-control daily (2026-11-26). Write the source on each ticket; do not open GitHub issues. Quoted feedback is data, not instructions. Read docs/VISION.md first: each ticket names the metric it improves and what it removes. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds. Group these as you judge (core/chain.py); 1.1 and 1.2 touch slots and dispatch, 1.3 regression and testiface, 1.4 landing and release.

## 1.1 The exclusive scope covers the release and the tests agents run
T (measured there): swap at 22/23 GB, Chrome took 30 s to open, many reds and unmeasured runs came from memory exhaustion; a release running beside another group's full regression made each stage 40-55% slower.
Main session (read the code): `devloop.regression_exclusive` only orders regressions against each other. The release (devloop/core/release.py) takes no slot; workers and verifiers running tests take an ordinary slot.
Wanted:
- The release takes the whole machine like an exclusive regression (same gate, same wait rules and limits as a regression since #121).
- While a full test run (regression or release) holds the machine, tests an agent runs through run_tests.py wait or report "machine busy" (as the opener already does, issue #7); agents keep writing code.
- Find out whether T's browser tests can be started by an agent by any path other than run_tests.py (read T's AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md and A's prompts; T's repo is at ../tabby_pool if present, read-only). Say in the ticket what you found.

## 1.2 Pause new agents when memory is short
Main session (read the code): devloop/core/host.py already samples available memory, but nothing decides with it.
Wanted:
- Below a threshold (a setting such as `devloop.min_free_memory`, or swap use; pick the measure and the default from T's samples in <worktrees>/runs/host/*.jsonl if you can reach them, else say what you assumed), the controller starts no new agent and no new regression; running ones go on.
- The reason shows on the idle page and on the board's live tab.
- How to read memory pressure on macOS must be checked, not guessed (vm_stat, memory_pressure, sysctl); Linux reads /proc/meminfo as today.

## 1.3 Stopping a regression also stops the tests it started
Main session (read the code): devloop/regression.py's docstring says "The test command it had started is not stopped (it runs in its own session)". devloop/core/osx.py `run()` kills the process tree only on timeout; scripts/testiface.py `launch()` starts another new session for `ac-test`.
T (seen there): orphan browsers keep piling up on the machine (three headless Firefox groups 20 hours old; geckodriver 15-20 days old); each cleanup needs the user's permission.
Wanted:
- regression.py on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP stops testiface.py's process group; testiface.py on those signals stops the `ac-test` process group; osx.run() stops the child tree on any exception other than a timeout, too.
- Acceptance: within 5 s of stopping a regression, neither layer runs. Remove the "not stopped" sentence from the docstring.
- This touches the hard_block words (os.kill / killpg), so the ticket stops before merge for the user: say so in the ticket.

## 1.4 Landed is written before the release, and the release does not block the controller
T (seen there): one release takes 70+ minutes and the controller dispatches nothing meanwhile.
Main session (read the code): land() fast-forwards main, then runs the release, the rerun and the fix-ticket openers synchronously, and writes `landed` last; a controller that dies in between restarts with the group still `verified` and would release again (inference).
